THE NOAA COOPERATIVE SCIENCE CENTER FOR COASTAL AND MARINE ECOSYSTEMS (CCME) IS LED BY FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY.  PARTNER INSTITUTIONS INCLUDE: BETHUNE COOKMAN UNIVERSITY; CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY MONTEREY BAY; JACKSON STATE UNIVERSITY; TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY-CORPUS CHRISTI; AND, THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS RIO GRANDE VALLEY.  CCME TRAINS STUDENTS, PRIMARILY FROM HISTORICALLY EXCLUDED COMMUNITIES AND UNDERREPRESENTED IN NOAA-MISSION SCIENCES.  CCME ALSO CONDUCTS TRAINING INCLUDING COLLABORATIONS WITH NOAA RESEARCHERS AND MANAGERS AT  THE NATIONAL OCEAN SERVICE, NOAA RESEARCH, AND OTHER NOAA  OFFICES. USING AN INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, CCME PREPARES STUDENTS TO BE CANDIDATES FOR THE FUTURE STEM WORKFORCE BY PROVIDING STUDENTS WITH THE SKILLS TO ADDRESS ISSUES AFFECTING MARINE AND COASTAL COMMUNITIES. CCME CONDUCTS RESEARCH FOCUSED ON THREE FOCAL AREAS - PLACE-BASED CONSERVATION, COASTAL RESILIENCE, AND COASTAL INTELLIGENCE.  FOR CCME EDUCATION AND TRAINING, AWARD-SUPPORTED STUDEN

THE NOAA COOPERATIVE SCIENCE CENTER FOR LIVING MARINE RESOURCES - II (NOAA LMRCSC - II) IS COMPOSED OF A CONSORTIUM OF SEVEN INSTITUTIONS, WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND EASTERN SHORE AS THE LEAD INSTITUTION. THE PARTNER INSTITUTIONS ARE: DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY; HAMPTON UNIVERSITY; OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY; SAVANNAH STATE UNIVERSITY; THE UNIVERSITY OF MIAMI; AND, THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE.  LMRCSC PREPARES STUDENTS PRIMARILY FROM HISTORICALLY EXCLUDED COMMUNITIES AND UNDERREPRESENTED IN NOAA-MISSION SCIENCE FOR CAREERS IN RESEARCH, MANAGEMENT, AND PUBLIC POLICY THAT SUPPORT THE SUSTAINABLE HARVEST AND CONSERVATION OF THE NATION'S LIVING MARINE RESOURCES. THE COOPERATIVE SCIENCE CENTER RESEARCH FOCUSES ON MANAGEMENT OF FISHERIES RESOURCES, WITH COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS BETWEEN ITS PARTNER INSTITUTIONS AND NOAA IN AREAS SUCH AS STOCK ASSESSMENT, ESSENTIAL FISH HABITAT, RESOURCE ECONOMICS, AND SUSTAINABLE AQUACULTURE.
